body:
Thanks for raising this issue!

> Some also used the fact that < and > were not escaped in attribute values, which was fixed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/6362. But mXSS attacks are likely still possible.

That's definitely the case, here's an example of mXSS which _didn't_ rely on the fact that `<` and `>` used to not be escaped.

> It's not clear if it's still possible to change this, or if there's web content that depends on style, script or title in SVG to have normal parsing. Also, changing this would likely cause some problems until all parsers agree on the new parsing. But in the long term it may be better if we can solve the mXSS vector completely.

So I think the way to go here would be to add a use counter that would trigger if `<style>`, `<script>`, `<title>` and other similar tags would have anything else as children than text nodes?

> That's definitely the case, here's an example of mXSS which _didn't_ rely on the fact that `<` and `>` used to not be escaped.

Did you mean to add a link?

> So I think the way to go here would be to add a use counter that would trigger if `<style>`, `<script>`, `<title>` and other similar tags would have anything else as children than text nodes?

Yes, or (except for `title` and `textarea`) if they use character references. CDATA sections (which are inserted as normal text) are also of interest.

> Did you mean to add a link?

Ah, sorry, yes. Here it is: https://research.securitum.com/mutation-xss-via-mathml-mutation-dompurify-2-0-17-bypass/

After looking at the data, I'd propose:

- `textarea`, `xmp`, `iframe`, `noembed`, `noframes` and `plaintext` break out of foreign content, like `p`.
- `title`, `style`, `script` and `noscript` stay SVG/MathML elements, parsed as RCDATA. `noscript` can't break out, because Google Tag Manager and WordPress put it in hidden SVG sprites. Comments and PIs inside them are still nodes (for framework markers, and #12118), but the element's end tag ends them. With today's escaped serialization this round-trips, and current parsers read it back the same way.
- `<![CDATA[` and `]]>` are dropped inside them, but the end tag still ends the element. That's a difference from XML and from CDATA in other foreign elements.
- Self-closing tags keep today's behavior.
- HTML `plaintext` stays PLAINTEXT.

AI summary of the research ([zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397](https://github.com/zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397)):

> The corpus is the HTTP Archive 2026-10-01 mobile crawl, 15,360,905 root pages. A regex scan found candidate SVG/MathML elements, and html5lib patched for the proposal parsed those pages today's way and the new way. Samples were checked by loading pages live, in a Firefox build with a pref. A Common Crawl sample (256,037 pages) agrees.
>
> | Part of the proposal | Root pages that parse differently | Effect |
> |---|---|---|
> | `title`, `style`, `script`, `noscript` as RCDATA, comments and PIs kept | 348 (0.0023%) | markup inside them becomes text, mostly in `<title>` tooltips; none of 100 sampled pages looked different (the build drops comments instead, which renders the same) |
> | … of which a `<style>`/`<title>` is never closed | 5 | on 3, the rest of the page becomes text |
> | the six breaking out | 1 | an SVG `iframe` embedding YouTube starts loading |
>
> - greenplaceamsterdam.com, agua-eshop.com, pleasewaittobeseated.com: today `</defs>` or `</svg>` closes the SVG `<style>`. Under the proposal it swallows the rest of the page ([image](https://github.com/zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397/blob/main/review/unclosed-style-greenplaceamsterdam.png), [image](https://github.com/zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397/blob/main/review/unclosed-style-agua-eshop.png); today on the left).
> - petrovskaja-school.ru: the SVG `iframe` would start loading its YouTube embed.
> - `<![CDATA[` (~7k pages) and self-closing tags (~6k pages) in these elements parse as today.
> - Framework comment markers in SVG `<title>`/`<style>`, such as React's `<!-- -->`, stay comment nodes, so those pages keep today's DOM (hydration not checked in a browser).
>
> The [README](https://github.com/zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397#readme) also covers the other options considered: tokenizing exactly like HTML (1.47% of pages, mostly Wix), RCDATA with comments as text or dropped, other choices for `noscript` and `script`, and ending HTML `plaintext` at `</plaintext>`.

Rough plan to fix this:

1. Add parse errors where parsing would change with the proposal (["rcdata-c"](https://github.com/zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397#readme) plus breakout).
2. Make a draft spec PR for it, with tests. This includes changing the content model of SVG `title` in HTML documents from phrasing content to text, comments and PIs, since it would no longer be an HTML integration point.
3. Add an opt-in mode to the spec's HTML serializer whose output parses the same before and after the change. It drops SVG/MathML `textarea`, `xmp`, `iframe`, `noembed`, `noframes` and `plaintext` elements anywhere, since they would break out. Inside SVG/MathML `title`, `style`, `script` and `noscript`, it omits comments and PIs that contain the element's end tag and flattens element children to text.
4. Boil the ocean: fix server-side sanitizers as per [the transition-risk notes](https://github.com/zcorpan/foreign-rawtext-compat-11397#transition-risk-for-stored-and-server-side-sanitized-content), using the serializer mode (step 3) where it helps.
5. Ship it in one browser (Firefox).
6. Land the spec PR, implement in other browsers.

This was discussed at WHATNOT: @mfreed7 said Chromium would be willing to follow if I did the boiling, and @annevk wasn't sure it was worth it but also didn't want to stand in the way (please correct if needed).
